Practical smoke samples are not a broad capability benchmark.
Historical Strata throughput is not a matched-workload comparison.
The workstation's GPU link trains at PCIe 5.0 x4 in an x16 slot (11.3 GB/s host-to-device); prefill streaming, swaps and loading are bandwidth-limited by it.
The 32,768-token MTP draft vocabulary lowers first-draft acceptance on prose (74.1% versus 82.9% with the full lm_head on the speculative test prompts).
Prefill CPU/GPU expert splits follow the startup cost measurement, so separate processes round prefill differently; results repeat exactly within a process.

The RTX 5090 also drives the desktop: Hyprland takes the GPU about 300 times per second for ~1.2 ms time slices (20-29% of decode time measured inside fngine's context; pausing Hyprland made fixed-placement G1 decode steps 28-30% shorter). Every throughput number includes it.
Adaptive placement follows the routing of the running workload; the first steps of a new topic (or a new process) run with the startup ranking until swaps catch up (up to four per step).

Elastic expert slots are vacated as a sequence's context grows (a step or prefill chunk reaching their bytes) and refilled only by adaptive swaps after a new or truncated sequence; long contexts therefore run with fewer GPU experts, as before.
Fifth-pass paired throughput has mixed signs and substantial variance. Only the exact-width GR kernel improvement is established; no across-the-board whole-model speedup is claimed.

An earlier fifth-pass speculative test aborted in CUDA graph instantiation with an allocation error. Later uninstrumented full suites passed, but the allocator failure's root cause was not proven. The root-owned 26.5 GiB diagnostic core requires privileged cleanup; its exact path and command are recorded in perf-2026-10/round5.json.
